say: Today's big idea: eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
An eigenvector is a nonzero vector with a special relationship to the matrix A.
Here it is. Multiplying by A gives back the same vector, only scaled by lambda.
You can see that in the picture: v and A v lie on the same line.
So how do we find lambda?
It comes from moving everything to one side: A minus lambda I, times v, equals zero.
A nonzero v can only exist if this matrix is singular, which is why v lives in its null space.
Let me clear the board and summarise.
Solve the determinant equation to get every lambda.

text: then solve (A - λI)v = 0 for each λ
say: Then solve for v, once per eigenvalue.
